title: ByteWolf Vision Summary v0.1
description: The consumer-facing roll-up of one camera frame's detections and tracks. It is the stable, versioned contract a consumer reads instead of the Vision internals: the source, the frame, the producing model, freshness, and a bounded list of detection identities. Observation-only; no command, no flight authority. See brain/vision/canonical.py.

contract_version.description: Pins the meaning of every field below.

observed_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC, with an offset. When the frame was captured; age is measured from here.

max_age_s.description: How long this summary stays usable after observed_at. Past it it is stale and must not be acted on.

validity.description: 'valid': trustworthy at observed_at. 'invalid': measured but not trusted. 'missing': no frame was analysed. 'stale' is derived by the consumer from age.

frame.description: The frame's pixel dimensions, so a consumer can interpret each bounding box.

detections.description: A bounded list of detection identities in this frame. May be shorter than detection_count when the producer caps it; a consumer must read detection_count for the true total, not len(detections).

event_id.description: Optional link to the full DetectionEvent, when one was published.

tracker_id.description: Present only for a detection carried across frames under a stable track.

detection_count.description: The true number of detections in the frame. Distinct from len(detections), which may be capped: a consumer must not read absence of a listed detection as 'nothing there'.
